blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 1

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below.

Salt

Salt is the common name for the substance sodium chloride (NaCl), which occurs in the form of transparent cubic crystals. Although salt is most familiar as a food supplement, less than 5% of the salt produced worldwide is used for that purpose. About 70% is utilized by the chemical industry, mostly as a source of chlorine. Salt is also used for countless other purposes, such as removing snow and ice from roads, softening water, preserving food, and stabilizing soils for construction.

The earliest humans obtained their salt from natural salt concentrations, as well as from meat. Those people who lived near the ocean may also have obtained it by chewing seaweed or from the natural evaporation of small pools of seawater. Meat became a more important source of salt as hunting was developed, as did milk when sheep, goats, horses, camels, reindeer, and cattle were domesticated. Even today, certain peoples—such as the Bedouin of the Middle Eastern deserts and the Maasai of East Africa—use no other forms of salt.

As agriculture developed, leading to a diet consisting mostly of plants, it became necessary to devise ways of obtaining salt in greater amounts. The earliest method of salt production employed by humankind was the evaporation of seawater using the heat of the sun. This method was particularly suited to hot, arid regions near the ocean or near salty lakes, and is still used in those areas. Solar evaporation was soon followed by the quarrying of exposed masses of rock salt, which quickly developed into the mining of underground deposits of salt. Two thousand years ago, the Chinese began using wells to reach underground pools of salt water, some of which were more than one kilometer deep.

In areas where the climate did not allow solar evaporation, salt water was poured on burning wood or heated rocks to boil it. The salt left behind was then scraped off. During the time of the Roman Empire, shallow lead pans were used to boil salt water over open fires to extract the salt. Later, in the Middle Ages, these were replaced with iron pans which were heated with coal. In the 1860s, a procedure known as the Michigan process was invented, in which salt water was heated by steam running through pipes immersed in the water. This process is still used to produce certain types of salt.

Nowadays, salt is collected from two sources: rock salt and brine. Rock salt is simply crystallized salt, also known as halite. It is the result of the evaporation of ancient oceans millions of years ago. Underground salt deposits are usually discovered by prospectors searching for water or oil. When salt is detected, a diamond-tipped, hollow drill is used to take several regularly spaced core samples throughout the area. These are analyzed to determine if salt mining would be profitable. If the site is thought to be suitable, vertical tunnels are sunk into the center of the salt deposit. Then a machine resembling a gigantic chain saw is used to cut a long horizontal slot through the salt, in a procedure known as undercutting. A series of holes are then drilled into the salt with an electric drill, and the holes are filled with explosives such as dynamite. Cutting and blasting are repeated in a pattern that leaves salt pillars standing to support the roof of the mining area. This is known as the room-and-pillar method and is also used in coal mines. Once blasted, chunks of the rock salt are transported to an underground crushing area where smaller pieces are collected via a metal grill and larger pieces are crushed in a rotating cylinder. Finally, redundant matter is extracted from the rock salt, in what is known as picking.

Brine is water containing a high concentration of salt. The most obvious source of brine is the ocean, but it can also be obtained from salty lakes such as the Dead Sea and from underground pools of salt water. Most brine is processed by a multi-effect vacuum evaporator. This device consists of three or more closed metal cylinders. Brine is first treated to remove chemical compounds. It then fills the bottom of the cylinders. The brine in the first cylinder passes through tubes heated by steam. The brine boils and its steam enters the next cylinder. In each cylinder, the condensation of steam causes the pressure inside to drop. A material called slurry forms at the bottom of the cylinders and goes into a tank. The slurry is then filtered to remove excess brine, dried, and passed through screens to sort the salt particles according to how large they are.

Specifications for salt vary widely according to the intended use. Salt intended for human consumption must be much purer than salt used for melting snow and ice on roads, but salt used for certain scientific purposes may need to be even purer.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?

In boxes 1–5 on your answer sheet, write:

  • TRUE if the statement agrees with the information
  • FALSE if the statement contradicts the information
  • NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this

1 The chemical industry makes use of the majority of salt produced globally.

2 In ancient times, people were only able to get salt from a single source.

3 Salt production through quarrying rock salt was common before the solar evaporation method of producing salt.

4 Two thousand years ago, the Chinese were quick to develop the equipment needed to mine underground.

5 At the time of the Roman Empire, salt was removed from salt water by heating the water in a type of pan.

Complete the notes below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

The production of rock salt

  • samples of the salt are collected with the aid of a drill
  • the salt is analysed to see if mining should go ahead
  • vertical tunnels are sunk into the middle of the salt deposit
  • during a process called 6 , a machine is used to break into the salt
  • explosives are placed in the holes in the salt
  • after blasting, 7 of salt are left behind to hold the roof up
  • in an underground crushing area, small pieces of rock salt are gathered using a 8
  • the process of 9 removes any unwanted material from the rock salt

Complete the flow-chart below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

Obtaining salt from brine: the multi-effect vacuum evaporator

cylinders made of 10 are filled with brine
↓
11 heats the tube in the first cylinder
↓
the 12 in the cylinders falls due to condensation
↓
slurry collects in the cylinders and passes to a tank

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 1
passageNotes.text: 文章先定义盐（NaCl）并强调其用途结构：全球产盐中用于食用的不到 5%，约 70% 被化工行业消耗（尤其制氯），其余还用于除冰、软化水、食品保存和工程固土等场景。核心意思是“盐远不只是调味品”。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 2
passageNotes.text: 早期人类通过天然盐源、肉类获取盐；沿海人群还可通过海藻和海水蒸发残留摄盐。狩猎与畜牧发展后，肉和乳制品成为更重要盐来源。文中举例贝都因人与马赛人至今仍主要靠这类自然路径摄盐。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 3
passageNotes.text: 农业发展使饮食更偏植物，促使人类必须扩大盐产量。最早系统化方法是日晒蒸发海水，适用于炎热干旱沿海/盐湖地区。之后发展到采掘岩盐，再到地下盐矿开采。两千年前中国已通过深井获取地下盐卤，部分井深超过一公里。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 4
passageNotes.text: 在不适合日晒蒸发的地区，人们通过加热盐水取盐：先用燃木或热石，罗马时期使用浅铅锅，随后中世纪改铁锅并用煤加热。19 世纪 60 年代出现 Michigan 工艺，用蒸汽管加热盐水，这套思路至今仍用于某些盐产品。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 5
passageNotes.text: 现代岩盐采集流程较机械化：钻孔取样评估矿体价值，垂直巷道进入矿层中心，再以类似巨型链锯设备进行 undercutting；随后钻孔装药爆破，并保留盐柱支撑顶板（room-and-pillar）。爆后矿盐进入地下破碎区，小块经 metal grill 收集，最终通过 picking 去除杂质。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 6
passageNotes.text: 卤水来源包括海洋、盐湖与地下盐卤。主流处理设备是多效真空蒸发器：多个金属密闭圆筒中，首筒通过蒸汽加热管促使卤水沸腾，蒸汽进入后续筒体；凝结过程会使压力逐级下降，形成 slurry，随后过滤、干燥，并用 screens 按颗粒大小分级。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 7
passageNotes.text: 结尾强调“盐规格依用途而异”：食盐纯度要求高于道路融雪盐，而某些科学用途还要求更高纯度。

items.text:
题目：The chemical industry makes use of the majority of salt produced globally.
题目翻译：化工行业使用了全球生产盐的大部分。
答案：TRUE
解析：第1段给出约 70% 盐用于化工，明显超过一半，题干成立。

题目：In ancient times, people were only able to get salt from a single source.
题目翻译：古代人只能从单一来源获得盐。
答案：FALSE
解析：第2段列出天然盐源、肉类、海藻、海水蒸发等多种来源，不是单一来源。

题目：Salt production through quarrying rock salt was common before the solar evaporation method of producing salt.
题目翻译：通过采石式开采岩盐取盐的方法早于日晒蒸发法。
答案：FALSE
解析：第3段明确顺序是先日晒蒸发，之后才出现采石与地下开采，因此题干与原文顺序相反。

题目：Two thousand years ago, the Chinese were quick to develop the equipment needed to mine underground.
题目翻译：两千年前中国迅速开发了地下采矿所需设备。
答案：NOT GIVEN
解析：第3段只说中国开始利用深井获取地下盐卤，并未评价“开发速度是否快”，题干中的“quick”无证据支持。

题目：At the time of the Roman Empire, salt was removed from salt water by heating the water in a type of pan.
题目翻译：罗马帝国时期，人们通过在某种锅中加热盐水来提盐。
答案：TRUE
解析：第4段明确写到罗马时期使用浅铅锅在明火上煮盐水提盐，题干一致。

questionExplanations.text: 题目 1-5 答案依次为：TRUE、FALSE、FALSE、NOT GIVEN、TRUE。证据主要位于第1-4段，重点是用途比例、取盐来源多样性和工艺演进顺序。

items.text:
题目：During a process called ______, a machine is used to break into the salt.
题目翻译：在名为 ______ 的工序中，机器被用来切入盐层。
答案：undercutting
解析：第5段把“用类似链锯机器切开盐层”的步骤直接命名为 undercutting。

题目：After blasting, ______ of salt are left behind to hold the roof up.
题目翻译：爆破后会保留 ______ 盐体来支撑顶板。
答案：pillars
解析：第5段说明爆破模式会留下 salt pillars 支撑矿顶，对应 pillars。

题目：In an underground crushing area, small pieces of rock salt are gathered using a ______.
题目翻译：在地下破碎区，小块岩盐通过 ______ 收集。
答案：grill
解析：第5段原文为 “smaller pieces are collected via a metal grill”，关键词为 grill。

题目：The process of ______ removes any unwanted material from the rock salt.
题目翻译：______ 工序用于去除岩盐中的杂质。
答案：picking
解析：第5段末尾写道杂质去除步骤 called picking，答案为 picking。

questionExplanations.text: 题目 6-9 答案依次为：undercutting、pillars、grill、picking。都可在第5段岩盐开采流程中直接定位。

items.text:
题目：Cylinders made of ______ are filled with brine.
题目翻译：由 ______ 制成的圆筒被注入卤水。
答案：metal
解析：第6段说多效蒸发器由多个 closed metal cylinders 组成，因此答案是 metal。

题目：______ heats the tube in the first cylinder.
题目翻译：______ 为第一圆筒中的管道加热。
答案：steam
解析：第6段写第一圆筒中卤水通过蒸汽加热管被加热，关键词是 steam。

题目：The ______ in the cylinders falls due to condensation.
题目翻译：由于冷凝，圆筒内的 ______ 会下降。
答案：pressure
解析：第6段明确指出蒸汽冷凝会导致圆筒内部 pressure 下降。

题目：______ are used to separate salt particles by size.
题目翻译：使用 ______ 按颗粒大小分离盐粒。
答案：screens
解析：第6段末尾写到通过 screens 进行粒径分级，答案为 screens。

questionExplanations.text: 题目 10-13 答案依次为：metal、steam、pressure、screens。答案全部来自第6段卤水蒸发流程描述。
